title: Memoir
summary: A personal narrative unit for grades 9–12: six stages from a flash-forward lead to the “so what”, with checklists, a share board, grading and a memoir poster.

steps.caption: The student view. A memoir is built in six stages, mapped like a story arc.
Each stage explains the craft move, with a checklist beside the writing.

steps.text: My hands were shaking so hard the paper rattled. “Next up,” Ms. Rivera called, and every head in the room turned toward me. I thought about the first time I had stood up in front of people, when I was seven and forgot every word.

steps.caption: The checklist ticks itself as they write, and their work saves as they type.
The teacher dashboard. Every stage is a tile with its own rubric.
The rubric is on the grading screen, with each student’s writing beside it.

steps.text: Great flash-forward. The shaking paper puts us right there.

steps.caption: Scores and comments save on their own. Push grades to Canvas when you’re ready.
